fullPassage: In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. People ate it or rubbed it into injuries. They believed it could be used to treat coughs and headaches. However, mumia was not always embraced by the medical community. Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.

questions.passage: In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. People ate it or rubbed it into injuries. They believed it could be used to treat coughs and headaches. However, mumia was <u>not always embraced by the medical community</u>. Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 not always embraced by the medical community가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: embrace(받아들이다)를 부정한 'not always embraced'는 '늘 받아들여진 것은 아니었다', 즉 일부 전문가는 인정하지 않았다는 뜻
det.analysis:
밑줄 'not always embraced by the medical community'에서 embrace는 '받아들이다, 지지하다'예요. 여기에 not always(항상 ~인 것은 아닌)가 붙었으니 '의료계가 늘 지지한 것은 아니었다', 곧 일부는 반대했다는 뜻이에요.

① 일부 의사와 전문가들은 미라 약의 사용을 인정하지 않았다: 밑줄의 의미와 정확히 일치 ←정답

② 공식 승인을 받아 표준 치료가 되었다: '받아들여지지 않기도 했다'는 밑줄과 정반대 — 오답

③ 연구할 예산이 전혀 없었다: 예산 이야기는 밑줄과 무관 — 오답

④ 환자들 사이에서만 은밀히 거래되었다: '의료계'의 수용 여부와 다른 이야기 — 오답
det.tip: not always embraced = 늘 받아들여진 건 아님 → 일부는 반대

ch: 일부 의사와 전문가들은 미라 약의 사용을 인정하지 않았다.
미라 약은 의료계의 공식 승인을 받아 표준 치료가 되었다.
의료계는 미라 약을 연구할 예산이 전혀 없었다.
미라 약은 환자들 사이에서만 은밀히 거래되었다.

questions.passage: In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. People ate it or rubbed it into injuries. They believed it could be used to treat coughs and headaches. However, mumia was not always embraced by the medical community. Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view <u>this practice</u> as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 this practice가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: this practice = 앞 문장들에서 말한, 미라를 약으로 먹고 시신을 미라로 만들던 행위
det.analysis:
밑줄 'this practice(이 관행)'는 바로 앞 문장들의 내용을 가리켜요. 앞에서 사람들이 미라를 약으로 '먹고', 최근 사망자의 시신마저 미라로 '만들려' 했다고 나왔어요. 현대인은 그런 행위를 식인 풍습으로 볼 것이라는 흐름이에요.

① 약을 처방하는 행위: 식인으로 볼 대상이 아님 — 오답

② 병원에서 치료하는 행위: 밑줄이 가리키는 대상과 무관 — 오답

③ 무덤을 관광지로 개발하는 행위: 본문에 없는 내용 — 오답

④ 죽은 사람의 시신을 미라로 만들거나 미라를 약으로 먹는 행위: 앞 문장들이 말한 바로 그 관행 ←정답
det.tip: this practice = 미라를 먹고 시신을 미라로 만들던 앞의 행위

ch: 죽은 사람의 시신을 미라로 만들거나 미라를 약으로 먹는 행위

Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it __________ of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: a deadly poison=치명적인 독 / an unusual type=특이한 종류 / a common form=흔한 형태 / a religious symbol=종교적 상징
det.analysis:
빈칸은 '중세 유럽인들은 그것을 ___ 의 약으로 여겼다'예요. 현대인은 식인으로 보지만 중세인은 그것을 '특이하긴 해도 하나의 약'으로 받아들였다는 대조가 핵심이에요.

① a deadly poison: '치명적인 독'으로 여겼다면 약으로 쓸 이유가 없음 — 오답

② an unusual type: 중세인은 그것을 '특이한 종류'의 약으로 여김 ←정답

③ a common form: 미라 약은 '흔한' 것이 아니라 특이한 것이었으므로 반대 — 오답

④ a religious symbol: '종교적 상징'이 아니라 '약(medicine)'으로 봄 — 오답
det.tip: considered it ___ of medicine = 특이한 종류(an unusual type)의 약

questions.passage: In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. __________. They believed it could be used to treat coughs and headaches. However, mumia was not always embraced by the medical community. Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (8단어) (영어로)
'사람들은 그것을 먹거나 상처에 발랐다'
[조건] (1) ate, injuries, into, it, it, or, People, rubbed를 모두 사용
(2) 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: People ate it or rubbed it into injuries = 사람들은 그것을 먹거나 상처에 발랐다
det.analysis: 두 동작을 or로 잇는 문장이에요. People(사람들은) + ate it(그것을 먹었다) + or + rubbed it into injuries(상처에 발랐다). 'A를 B에 문지르다'는 rub A into B라서 rubbed it into injuries 순서가 돼요. 앞의 ate와 형태를 맞춰 rubbed(과거형)로 써요. = 8단어.
det.tip: rub A into B = A를 B에 문지르다 → rubbed it into injuries

questions.wa: People ate it or rubbed it into injuries
accept: People ate it or rubbed it into injuries

questions.passage: Medieval Europeans considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually __________ (stop) prescribing mumia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: stop(멈추다) → stopped. 과거의 일이므로 과거형이고, 짧은 모음+자음으로 끝나 p를 하나 더 붙여 stopped
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 15세기 이후의 일을 과거로 서술하고 있어요. 그래서 동사 stop을 과거형으로 바꿔요.

stop은 '단모음(o) + 자음(p)'으로 끝나는 1음절 단어라, 과거형을 만들 때 마지막 자음 p를 한 번 더 쓰고 -ed를 붙여 stopped가 돼요.

또 'stop + 동명사(prescribing)'는 '~하던 것을 멈추다'라는 뜻이라, 의사들이 처방하던 것을 '멈췄다(stopped)'가 자연스러워요.
det.tip: stop → stopped (자음 하나 더 + ed), stop + V-ing = ~하던 것을 멈추다

'미라 약은 의료계에서 항상 받아들여진 것은 아니었다'
[조건] (1) always, by, community, embraced, medical, mumia, not, the, was를 모두 사용
(2) 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: mumia was not always embraced by the medical community = 미라 약은 의료계에서 항상 받아들여진 것은 아니었다
det.analysis:
미라 약(mumia)이 '받아들여지는' 대상이므로 「be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)」수동태로 써요: was embraced(받아들여졌다). 행위자는 by the medical community(의료계에 의해)로 붙여요.

'항상 ~인 것은 아니다'는 부분부정이라 not always를 be동사(was)와 과거분사(embraced) 사이에 넣어요: was not always embraced. = mumia was not always embraced by the medical community(9단어).
det.tip: 수동태 was + p.p. + by ~, 부분부정 not always → was not always embraced by
